beats.text: Your phone could fly to the Moon, NASA did it with way less.
In 1969, Apollo 11 landed two humans on the Moon.

props.prompt: black and white grainy footage of lunar module on moon surface, 1960s

beats.bg: grainy black and white lunar surface

beats.text: The computer only had about 4 kilobytes of RAM.
But here's the thing, they didn't even type code.
beats.bg: old mechanical typewriter keys close up

beats.text: Women literally knitted the software by hand into copper wire.
It was called rope memory, woven by hand.
beats.bg: dense bundle of red copper wires

beats.text: Your phone has way more power than that.

props.fact: Your phone has way more power than that.

beats.text: We took that incredible manual precision for granted for decades.
Respect to the women who literally knitted software.
Would you trust a hand-woven computer to save your life?
